beginner_version.found: Tiny separate things: only the stars, a sparse scatter of about thirty dots that one dotting or splatter mark makes; no houses, people or windows. Textures of hundreds of items: none (busy measured 0.2% fine texture, one tile on the lantern's ring). Detail inside big shapes: the swirled sky, the wood grain and the drift strokes are each one repeated mark. Parts: sky, moon, stars, pines, snow, glow, post and rails, snow caps, lantern: about four distances, and close to the budget of 8 once small pieces are grouped.
beginner_version.why: The picture is already a loose, simple painting at a beginner's level of detail; a beginner version would only cost a render and could change the lantern.

canvas_fit.lost: about 11%: a thin strip of snowy sky and drift at the left edge and the end of the fence rails at the right edge
canvas_fit.why: No canvas was named, so fit-canvas picked the standard size closest to the 3:2 photo (12x16, landscape) and cropped it; the lantern, post and glow stay whole.

photo_prep.subject: A brass lantern glowing orange, hanging from a bracket on a weathered wooden fence post, over snowy drifts at night, with a full moon, stars and dark pines behind.
photo_prep.why: The whole image is the painting: no bars, borders, text or frame.
